item.title: Russian memo floats return to dollar system in pitch to Trump
item.description:
The Kremlin has drafted an internal memo outlining proposals for sweeping economic cooperation with the United States that includes a return to the dollar system, according to market sources, as Moscow seeks to capitalize on the Trump administration's transactional approach to foreign policy.

The high-level document, drafted this year, identifies seven areas where Russian and American economic interests could align, including cooperation on fossil fuels, joint investments in natural gas and offshore Arctic oil extraction, and opportunities for American companies in critical raw materials. The proposals are contingent on a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

item.title: Europe overtakes US as Ukraine's largest military backer, study finds
item.description:
Europe has overtaken the United States as Ukraine's largest military backer for the first time since June 2022, according to new data from the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, marking a seismic shift in Western support as the war enters its fifth year.

The German think tank's Ukraine Support Tracker, published on February 11, shows that European nations have now provided €72 billion in total military aid to Kyiv, compared with €65 billion from Washington. The reversal follows a near-total collapse in American support under the Trump administration, with U.S. military aid plummeting 99% in 2025.

item.title: Iran reinforces key nuclear site as US diplomacy continues
item.description:
Fresh satellite imagery reveals Iran is hardening defenses at an underground tunnel complex near Natanz, its most critical remaining nuclear facility, as diplomatic negotiations with the United States continue and military tensions in the region escalate.

Images captured on February 10 by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) show concrete being poured at tunnel entrances and heavy construction equipment actively reinforcing the site at Kolang-Gaz La Mountain, widely known as Pickaxe Mountain, located roughly two kilometers south of the Natanz enrichment facility.

The fortification efforts come eight months after U.S. and Israeli airstrikes struck multiple Iranian nuclear sites during the June 2025 conflict. The United States conducted Operation Midnight Hammer on June 22, 2025, targeting the Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan nuclear facilities with bunker-buster bombs and Tomahawk cruise missiles. Pickaxe Mountain was notably not among the facilities targeted, though analysts say Iran has since accelerated construction there as its most important undamaged nuclear asset.

item.title: Russia dismisses Ukraine claim it can't run Zaporizhzhia plant
item.description:
Ukraine's state nuclear company has warned that a restart of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant under Russian control risks a nuclear accident, prompting a sharp rebuke from Moscow's atomic agency, which dismissed the allegations as unfounded.

Pavlo Kovtoniuk, acting chairman of Energoatom, told Reuters on Tuesday that Russia lacks the necessary equipment and spare parts to safely operate Europe's largest nuclear facility. "Russia will not be able to restart the station. The main equipment and the control, protection, and monitoring systems are all Ukrainian," Kovtoniuk said. "Without spare parts and without the project, the station simply cannot be operated."

item.title: European stocks reverse from record highs as AI fears grip markets
item.description:
European stock markets climbed to fresh all-time highs on Thursday morning as investors cheered positive corporate earnings from luxury and industrial companies, but gains faded later in the session as renewed fears about artificial intelligence disruption dragged global equities lower.

The pan-European STOXX 600 surged 0.7% to 625.86 points in early trading, setting a new record, according to Reuters. France's CAC 40 led regional benchmarks with a 1.4% rise. However, the rally reversed by the close, with the STOXX 600 ending down 0.5% as U.S. markets tumbled, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: Astronomers find 'inside out' solar system with rocky outer planet
item.description:
An international team of astronomers has discovered a planetary system that challenges long-held theories about how planets form, with a rocky world orbiting farther from its star than two gas-rich planets. The discovery, published Wednesday in the journal Science, reveals the first evidence of a planet that may have formed in a gas-depleted environment.

The system orbits LHS 1903, a red dwarf star located 116 light-years from Earth. Using the European Space Agency's CHEOPS satellite, researchers led by Dr. Thomas Wilson of the University of Warwick detected a fourth planet at the system's outer edge—one that unexpectedly appears to be rocky rather than gaseous.

item.title: NASA tests repaired Artemis II rocket after hydrogen leak
item.description: NASA is loading liquid hydrogen into its Space Launch System rocket at Kennedy Space Center on Thursday in a previously unannounced test to verify seal repairs following a leak that halted a critical countdown rehearsal earlier this month. The test marks the latest milestone as the agency works toward launching Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the Moon since the Apollo era.

item.title: Anthropic closes $30B round, valuing AI firm at $380B
item.description:
Anthropic announced Thursday that it has completed a $30 billion Series G funding round, valuing the San Francisco-based AI company at $380 billion post-money. The deal stands as the second-largest private technology fundraise in history, trailing only OpenAI's $40 billion round led by SoftBank in March 2025.

Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC and Coatue Management led the financing, with co-lead investments from D.E. Shaw, Dragoneer Investment Group, Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, ICONIQ, and Abu Dhabi's MGX, according to a GIC press release and Bloomberg reporting. Strategic investors Microsoft and Nvidia, which committed up to a combined $15 billion in Anthropic last November, participated alongside Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, and Altimeter Capital.

item.title: Europe's most powerful rocket launches Amazon satellites in maiden flight
item.description:
Europe's most powerful rocket successfully reached orbit for the first time on Wednesday, carrying 32 satellites for Amazon.com, Inc.'s Leo broadband internet constellation in a launch that marks a new chapter for the continent's space ambitions.

The Ariane 64 lifted off at 16:45 UTC from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, deploying its payload to low-Earth orbit in a mission lasting one hour and 54 minutes. The successful debut flight confirms Europe's heavy-lift launch capability and represents the first commercial customer mission for the Ariane 6 rocket family.

item.title: Trump repeals EPA climate finding as UN chief warns of 'new world disorder'
item.description:
The head of the United Nations climate body on Thursday urged countries to unite against what he called an "unprecedented threat" to international cooperation from pro-fossil fuel forces, delivering his stark assessment as the Trump administration took sweeping action to dismantle U.S. climate regulations.

Simon Stiell, Executive Secretary of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, addressed media in Istanbul alongside Turkey's incoming COP31 President Murat Kurum. The remarks came hours before President Donald Trump announced the repeal of a foundational scientific finding that underpinned federal authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions.

item.title: Iran fortifies nuclear sites amid US military buildup, images show
item.description:
Iran is reinforcing defenses at its key nuclear facilities as new satellite imagery reveals expanded fortifications and tunnel construction, with activity intensifying as diplomatic efforts with the United States continue alongside growing military pressure.

Fresh images analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security show tunnel entrances at the Isfahan nuclear complex being buried under soil, while construction activity continues at an underground facility near Natanz known as "Pickaxe Mountain," the BBC reported Wednesday. The developments come as President Donald Trump weighs deploying a second aircraft carrier to the Middle East and warns of "something very tough" if Iran fails to meet U.S. demands.

item.title: Deep Space Energy raises funds for lunar power technology
item.description:
From solar-powered orbital data centers to compact radioisotope generators, a wave of space-based power technologies is gaining momentum as governments and private companies race to harness energy beyond Earth's atmosphere.

SpaceX filed with the Federal Communications Commission in late January for approval to launch up to one million satellites that would function as orbital data centers, powered entirely by solar energy. The proposal represents the largest satellite constellation ever proposed and reflects growing interest in space as a solution to the surging energy demands of artificial intelligence computing. "By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance cost, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers," the company stated in its FCC filing.

item.title: Space-based solar power gains global momentum amid grid demands
item.description: New developments in space-based solar power and radioisotope energy systems are drawing fresh attention from governments, investors, and industry leaders who say these technologies could fundamentally transform how the world generates electricity. The renewed push comes as energy demand surges and countries race to develop clean, reliable power sources that operate independently of weather and daylight constraints.

item.title: DeepMind VP says decoding human genome is AI's next frontier
item.description:
Artificial intelligence could help decode the "recipe book of life" hidden inside human DNA and transform India into a global hub for cutting-edge scientific research, according to Google DeepMind's Vice President of Research Pushmeet Kohli.

In an interview with Moneycontrol, Kohli said AI's biggest potential lies in the democratization of science, allowing researchers with modest resources to compete with the world's best-funded laboratories. He pointed to AlphaFold, the Nobel Prize-winning protein structure prediction model developed by his teams, as proof of that transformative power. "All of that millions of dollars and multiple years has been transformed into one click," Kohli said, referring to how AlphaFold has reduced work that once took years to complete to mere seconds.

item.title: Bangladesh's BNP wins two-thirds majority in first post-uprising election
item.description:
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party has declared victory in the country's first parliamentary election since a Gen Z-led uprising ousted longtime ruler Sheikh Hasina in 2024, positioning party leader Tarique Rahman to become the next prime minister after 17 years in exile.

The BNP and its coalition partners secured approximately 212 of 299 contested seats, surpassing the two-thirds majority threshold, according to local television reports and preliminary Election Commission data. The Islamist party Jamaat-e-Islami and its allies captured around 70 seats, with party leader Shafiqur Rahman conceding defeat and pledging to pursue "constructive politics" rather than obstructionist opposition.

item.title: Norway charges ex-PM Jagland with corruption over Epstein ties
item.description:
Former Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjørn Jagland was formally charged with gross corruption on Thursday, February 12, as investigators probe his ties to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Norwegian police searched three of Jagland's properties and seized evidence after the Council of Europe lifted his diplomatic immunity just one day earlier.

Økokrim, Norway's economic crimes unit, confirmed that Jagland now faces charges of gross corruption—a serious category under Norwegian law—following allegations that he accepted benefits from Epstein between 2011 and 2018. The 75-year-old denies any criminal liability and has pledged to cooperate with the investigation, according to his lawyer Anders Brosveet.

item.title: China completes first at-sea rocket booster recovery
item.description:
China successfully conducted a dual flight test of its next-generation Long March-10 carrier rocket and Mengzhou crewed spacecraft on February 11, marking what the China Manned Space Agency called "major breakthroughs" in the country's ambitious plan to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030.

The test at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in Hainan Province achieved several firsts for China's space program, including the nation's first maximum dynamic pressure abort test of a crewed spacecraft and the first at-sea recovery of both a rocket booster and a spacecraft return capsule.

item.title: SpaceX Crew-12 cleared to launch to ISS on Friday morning
item.description:
Four astronauts are set to blast off to the International Space Station early Friday morning, ending a monthlong period in which the orbiting laboratory operated with a skeleton crew following the first medical evacuation in NASA's history.

NASA and SpaceX received a "go" to proceed with the Crew-12 launch countdown on Thursday, targeting liftoff at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Weather forecasters issued an improved outlook with a 90% chance of acceptable conditions at launch time.

item.title: Study finds Yangtze fishing ban reversed 70 years of decline
item.description:
A sweeping 10-year commercial fishing ban on China's Yangtze River has begun to reverse decades of ecological decline, with fish biomass more than doubling and endangered species showing signs of recovery, according to new research published Thursday in the journal Science.

The study, led by Professor Chen Yushun from the Institute of Hydrobiology at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, evaluated fish communities across 57 river reaches between 2018 and 2023, comparing conditions before and after the ban took effect in January 2021. Researchers found a 209 percent increase in overall fish biomass and a 13 percent increase in species richness.

item.title: Global tech stocks slide as AI disruption fears spread
item.description:
Asian equities retreated from record highs on Friday as a fresh wave of concern over artificial intelligence's disruptive potential swept through global markets, triggering sharp losses in technology stocks from Tokyo to Mumbai.

The selloff began on Wall Street Thursday, where the S&P 500 fell 1.6% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2% as investors fled software and tech shares perceived as vulnerable to AI-driven automation, according to Bloomberg. The rout spread to Asia on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 falling 1.2%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index declining 1.7%, and the Shanghai Composite shedding 1.3%.
